1.note: Jeremiah is using the phrase translated as **And the word of Yahweh came to me, saying,** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event. Alternate translation: [And again Yahweh gave me a message to deliver for him, telling me]

2.note: Yahweh is using **take to you a wife** as a common expression of the culture to mean “marry a woman.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You shall not marry a woman]

3.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 2:5.

4.note: Yahweh is using **deaths of diseases** as a common expression of the culture to mean “deaths that deadly diseases cause.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They will die because of deadly diseases]

The expressions **They shall not be lamented** and **they shall not be buried** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use those forms, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [No one will lament them and no one will bury them]

Here, **the sword** represents war. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and by war and by famine they shall be consumed]

The expression **they shall be consumed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [they shall perish]
See how you translated this expression in 7:33.

5.note: A **house of a funeral meal** is a kind of house where people gathered to eat and drink together in honor of someone who had died. If your readers would not be familiar with what a house of a funeral meal is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a house where people are mourning someone who has died]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if his **peace** were an object that he had **taken away** from this people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I no longer give this people my peace]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **peace**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the peaceful conditions I provided]
See how you translated **the declaration of Yahweh** in 1:8. This also occurs in verses 11, 14, and 16 of this chapter.

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and I have taken away my covenant faithfulness and my mercies]

The terms **covenant faithfulness** and **mercies** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [my unfailing kindness]

6.note: Yahweh is using the adjectives **great** and **small** as nouns to mean certain kinds of people. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [important people and unimportant people]

Yahweh is referring to all of the people of this land by naming two major components, **great** and **small**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [everyone]

The expression **They shall not be buried** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. This also occurs in verse 4. Alternate translation: [No one will bury them]

The pronoun **he** refers to anyone who would ordinarily mourn for a relative who had died. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [people shall not lament for them and no relative shall cut himself]

Cutting oneself was a symbolic action by which a person showed deep grief for someone who had died. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [people shall not cut themselves to show their grief]

Shaving the head bald was a symbolic action by which a person showed deep grief for someone who had died. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [and people shall not shave their heads bald to show their grief for the dead]

7.note: Yahweh is using **break bread** as a common expression of the culture to mean “provide a meal.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [shall they serve a funeral meal for them]

The pronoun **him** refers to a person who is mourning, not to the person who has died. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [to comfort the mourning person for the one who has died]
Here, **a cup** represents the drink that a cup contains. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [consoling wine]

8.note: Yahweh is using **the house of a feast** as a common expression of the culture to mean “a place where people are holding a banquet.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a place where people are holding a banquet]

9.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 6:6.

Yahweh is using **Behold me causing to cease** to indicate that he is about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now I am about to cause to cease]
The word **your** is plural here because Yahweh is addressing the people of Judah, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Here, **your eyes** represents your own sight. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. This also occurs in verse 17. Alternate translation: [before your very sight]

Yahweh is using **in your days** as a common expression of the culture to mean “during your lifetime.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [during your lifetime]
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:34.
See how you translated **the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride** in 7:34.

10.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the people mentioned earlier in this verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the people say to you, Jeremiah]

10.q: עַל־מֶה֩ דִבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה עָלֵ֨י⁠נוּ֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל־הָ⁠רָעָ֤ה הַ⁠גְּדוֹלָה֙ הַ⁠זֹּ֔את
10.note: The people are using **spoken all this great disaster** as a common expression of the culture to mean “forewarned of great disaster.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Why has Yahweh decreed that all this great disaster will come upon us]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **iniquity** and **sin**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and what wrong have we done and what evil have we committed]

11.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the ancestors of these people were their **fathers**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your forefathers]

Jeremiah is speaking of worshiping other gods as if it were **walking** behind them along a path. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they have started to worship other gods] or [and they have gone off to worship other gods]

12.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [to do more evil than your fathers did]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **stubbornness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [each one is walking after his own stubborn, evil heart]

Yahweh is using **to not listen to me** as a common expression of the culture to mean “to not obey me.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to disobey me]

13.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of sending his people into exile as if he would **throw** them out of the land. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [So I will forcibly send you far away from this land]

Yahweh is referring to all of the time by naming two extremes, **day** and **night**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all the time]

14.note: See how you translated this phrase in 7:32.

The expression **it shall no longer be said** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people will no longer say]
Following the custom of his culture, Jeremiah is swearing an oath and guaranteeing it by something that he holds sacred. Alternate translation: [I swear by Yahweh]

15.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [but rather it shall be said]
See how you translated the similar expression in 6:22.
See how you translated the similar expression in 15:10.

16.note: Yahweh is using **Behold me sending** as a common expression of the culture to mean that he was about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now I am about to send for many fishermen]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the enemies who will capture his people were **fishermen** who would catch them the way fishermen catch fish. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am sending for many enemies … and they shall capture them]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the enemies who will capture his people were **hunters** who would track them down the way hunters track down animals. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will send for many enemies and they shall search them out]

17.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the way people conduct their lives were the **ways** on which they travel. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all their conduct]

The expressions **they are not hidden** and **nor is their iniquity concealed** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use those forms, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [they cannot hide themselves from before my face, nor can they conceal their iniquity]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **hidden**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [they are clearly visible before my face]

17.q: לֹ֥א נִסְתְּר֖וּ מִ⁠לְּ⁠פָנָ֑⁠י וְ⁠לֹֽא־נִצְפַּ֥ן עֲוֺנָ֖⁠ם מִ⁠נֶּ֥גֶד עֵינָֽ⁠י
17.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [I see everything that they do and everything wrong that they do]
Here, **my face** represents my sight. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from my sight]

18.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the punishment he will bring on his people were a debt that he would **repay** to them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [But I will first punish them twice as much for]

The terms **iniquity** and **sin** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [their terrible wickedness]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the idols that his people worship were the lifeless **carcass** of an animal. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [with their lifeless, detestable idols]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the land of Israel were his **inheritance**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the land that belongs to me]

19.note: At this point Jeremiah begins to speak to Yahweh, although the text does not say so explicitly. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating who is speaking.

Here Jeremiah is speaking as if Yahweh were his **stronghold** and his **refuge**, that is, a fortified place to which he could run for safety. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my strength and the one who protects and keeps me safe]

Jeremiah is using **the day of trouble** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the time when trouble comes.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in the time when trouble comes]

Jeremiah is using **the ends of the earth** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the most distant places in the world.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from the most distant places in the world]

Here the nations are speaking as if the false gods that their ancestors handed down to them were property that they had **inherited**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [our fathers received from their ancestors only a lie]

The nations are leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [they have inherited worthlessness, and there is no profit in the things they inherited]

20.note: Jeremiah is using the question form to emphasize that no person is able to make real gods for himself. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Surely a man cannot make gods for himself!]

Jeremiah is not referring to a specific **man**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people]

The pronoun **they** refers to the idols or gods that a man might make for himself. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [But the gods that a man makes are not gods]

21.note: At this point Yahweh begins to speak again, although the text does not say so explicitly. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating who is speaking. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh responded,]
The pronoun **them** refers to the people of Judah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [I am making the people of Judah to know]

The terms **my hand** and **my might** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [my great power]
See how you translated this phrase in 3:17.
